components.role: Direct preference optimization is used as a preference-based fine-tuning method to align language models.
Code generation serves as the downstream capability being improved and evaluated.
Instruction following represents broader language model capabilities and tasks evaluated alongside code generation.

target_task.text: The combination targets code generation and instruction-following tasks.

limitation.text: Improving code generation typically relies on costly external resources such as powerful teacher models or reliable test units when obtaining reference solutions and test oracles is difficult.

combination.text: Direct preference optimization is combined with self-improving mechanisms using behavioral consensus to weight preference pairs, mitigating the impact of noisy self-generated supervision for code generation.
